requirements.statement: The last navigation item, 'Log out', links to /auth/sign-out on every frontend (animals, INS and plants) and is never marked as the current item. Log out ends the user's session with the service and sends them to Defra ID's sign-out page, headed 'You have signed out'. Opening the dashboard again afterwards asks them to sign in again with their user ID and password. A user who is not signed in and opens /auth/sign-out goes to the service root.
requirements.why: Ending a real session properly is an authentication behaviour the prototype cannot show. It already works and is proven end to end.
requirements.deltaNote: The item links to /auth/sign-out on all three frontends (repo-frontend-p1-161, repo-insfrontend-p4-010, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-010). trace-e2e-p1-041 to p1-046 show Log out reaching Defra ID's signed-out page and the dashboard asking for sign-in again; repo-insfrontend-p4-096 to p4-098 give the INS routes. Plants' sign-out itself is not proven end to end (repo-tests-p4-111-m1).

requirements.statement: The Manage account navigation item is a placeholder on every frontend (animals, INS and plants): it links to '#', leads nowhere, and is never marked as the current item.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows Manage account as a placeholder with no destination, which is what both frontends do today.
requirements.deltaNote: All three frontends link Manage account to '#' (repo-frontend-p1-013, repo-insfrontend-p4-009, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-009, trace-e2e-p15-003), as the prototype does (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-013).

requirements.statement: The first navigation item, Dashboard, links to the dashboard home of the set or frontend the page belongs to and is marked as the current item there. On the animals frontend it links to the set's own root (/live-animals for live-animals), which renders that set's own notification list, and stays current on every page inside a notification. On the plants frontend it links to /high-risk-plants and stays current on every notification page. On the INS frontend it links to / and is current only there. A Back, 'View dashboard' or 'Return to your dashboard' link that Design Release 2.1 sends to the overall dashboard goes to the set's own notification list.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the dashboard is the home: it is the Dashboard item's target and where the back link to the dashboard goes. The owner's 9 October afternoon and templates rulings keep each notification list in its own frontend at the set root, so the item and every return to the dashboard stay on the set root, which all three frontends already link to.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals Dashboard item goes to /live-animals and stays current inside a notification (repo-frontend-p1-010, p1-011, trace-e2e-p9-083); the plants item goes to /high-risk-plants and every notification path counts as the dashboard section (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-007, p1-043); the INS item goes to / and is current there (repo-insfrontend-p4-007). The list stays at each set root (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-086), so nothing moves. Where each return link points is built by the areas that own those pages; the germinal set's item has its own requirement.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend (both sets) and the INS frontend, the Address book navigation item takes the user to the INS frontend's address book at /address-book, and is marked as the current item on the address book and every page under it. From the animals frontend this is a link to the INS frontend's origin, and a user with no INS session goes through INS sign-in first. The plants item has its own requirement.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats the address book as part of one service. In the real services it is a shared capability in the INS frontend, a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals item already links out to the INS /address-book (trace-e2e-p9-084), and the INS item goes to /address-book and is current under it (repo-insfrontend-p4-008, p4-013).

requirements.statement: On every frontend, the service navigation items appear only to a signed-in user; a signed-out page shows the service name with no items.
requirements.why: The navigation leads to pages that need a signed-in user. This is a real authentication constraint, and it already works.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-007, repo-insfrontend-p4-005 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-006 hide the items when signed out.

requirements.statement: Every page on every frontend uses the GOV.UK service navigation component, which shows the service name 'Import notification service' in the navigation bar rather than in the header. On narrow screens the items collapse behind a 'Menu' button, and the navigation landmark is named 'Menu'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the service 'Import notification service' and uses GOV.UK service navigation with the name in the bar. Both frontends already do this.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-016 and trace-e2e-p15-001 show the service navigation component carrying the name on both frontends.

requirements.statement: The GOV.UK header logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ on every frontend, and the service name in the service navigation links to that page's dashboard home: /live-animals on live-animals pages of the animals frontend, /high-risk-plants on the plants frontend and / on the INS frontend. A page outside every set links the service name to the site root, which sends the user on to the default set. The germinal-products set's own home has its own requirement.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends both links to its index of design releases, prototype tooling with no counterpart in a real service (req-1681), so it names no real destination; with no DR1 judgement on the header links, the real frontends' targets are the only buildable ones and stand (c-214).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ on all three frontends (repo-frontend-p1-005, repo-insfrontend-p4-003, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-004), and the service name links to /live-animals on the animals frontend (repo-frontend-p1-006), /high-risk-plants on plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-005) and / on the INS frontend (repo-insfrontend-p4-004).

requirements.statement: The prototype's service index at /index is not built: its 'Prototypes' caption, its introduction, its four release cards (Design release 1, Design release 2, Design release 2.1, Testing version) with tags, 'What the journey contains' details and start buttons, and its title without the GOV.UK suffix.
requirements.why: The index is the prototype's own way to choose between design releases. A real service has one live version, so the page has no purpose there. It is prototype tooling, not part of the service the goal brings into line.

requirements.statement: The prototype kit's tooling is not built: the footer's 'Manage your prototype' and 'Clear data' links, and the kit's absence of custom Nunjucks filters and default session data.
requirements.why: These belong to the prototype kit, not to the service the design describes.

requirements.statement: The phase banner's feedback link is an email link to APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk on every frontend (animals, INS and plants), not the prototype's placeholder '#', and no /feedback route or survey URL is invented for it.
requirements.why: DR1 already judged this same difference, a placeholder feedback link in the design: the real link goes to the APHA service desk. That judgement outranks the prototype default.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-017, repo-insfrontend-p4-017 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-014 already mail APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk. The service team has still to confirm that mailbox as the feedback destination (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p1-009), and plants' own feedback address is parked with its service owner (req-layout-and-sign-in-013); that is for the report, not a build.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, every page's browser title reads the page name, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - '.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets no title pattern for its journey pages, so the animals frontend's existing pattern stands.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-001 and trace-animals-fit-p1-001 show the pattern.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, every page's browser title reads the page's title, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - ', as on the animals frontend.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one title pattern on every page; the INS frontend's pipe pattern is today's build, not a constraint the prototype cannot express. The 9 October afternoon ruling says this row is not the blocked summary information and goes ahead.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS frontend's titles read 'X | Import notification service' (repo-insfrontend-p4-001, trace-e2e-p15-004).

requirements.statement: When a page shows an error summary, its browser title starts with 'Error: ' ('Gwall: ' in Welsh) in front of the whole title, on every frontend.
requirements.why: This is the GOV.UK pattern for telling screen-reader users there are errors, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-002, repo-insfrontend-p4-002 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-002 add the prefix.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, page content sits in a two-thirds-width column by default, and a page that shows a table or other display content can use the full width.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays journey pages out in a two-thirds column. Both frontends already default to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-020, repo-insfrontend-p4-019 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-017 default to two-thirds.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, a page shows a GOV.UK back link labelled 'Back' ('Yn ôl' in Welsh), below the phase banner, only when it supplies a back-link target. No page shows breadcrumbs.
requirements.why: Each page gets one route back (the back link) and one route up (the service navigation). This already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-019, repo-insfrontend-p4-018 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-016 render the back link only when one is set.

requirements.statement: A journey page on the animals frontend names its section in a caption directly above its heading, such as 'About the consignment' above 'Main reason for import'. Where the question legend is visually hidden, the caption still sits directly above the page heading. The dashboard has an extra-large 'Dashboard' caption above its heading, and the overview has no caption. The plants frontend shows its journey pages' section caption the same way, in the large caption style above the heading, and leaves it out where a page has none.
requirements.why: Section captions already exist on the animals frontend. No source in this area's working set from Design Release 2.1 says otherwise.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-007 to p1-012 show the captions as rendered, and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-053 and p1-054 the plants captions. Each page's own caption wording against Design Release 2.1 belongs to that page's area.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, where a field's own copy gives no message, the shared default validation messages apply: 'Select a valid option', 'Enter a valid postcode', 'Enter a valid registration number', 'Enter a valid UK telephone number', 'Enter a valid date', 'Enter a real time, like 14:30', 'Enter a whole number', 'Enter N characters or fewer' and 'Enter a number between MIN and MAX'.
requirements.why: These are the fallbacks every page shares. Each page's own messages against Design Release 2.1 belong to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: The same defaults exist in all three frontends' shared copy (repo-frontend-p1-062 to p1-070, repo-insfrontend-p4-057 to p4-065, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-076 to p1-084).

requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends, a save that hits a recoverable backend failure re-renders the page with an alert banner titled 'There is a problem' that reads 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.' The banner sits at the top of the content column.
requirements.why: Real persistence can fail, which the prototype cannot express. The banner tells the user their answers are safe.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-021 and p1-022 render the banner on animals, and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-018 and p1-019 on plants.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, a page whose service call fails is re-rendered with status 500 and a notification banner with role 'alert', titled 'There is a problem' and reading 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: Real upstream services can fail, which the prototype cannot express, and the user is kept on the page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-020 and p4-021 render the banner.

requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends, a form post refused because the notification changed after the page was opened sends the user back to the same page. There an alert banner titled 'The notification has been updated' reads 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.'
requirements.why: Concurrent edits to a stored notification are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-023 and p1-024 implement the refusal and banner on animals, and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-020 and p1-021 on plants.

requirements.statement: A page inside a notification can show a shared strip above its content with the notification's status tag and its reference in bold: blue 'Draft', green 'Submitted' or grey 'Deleted' (the tag for an amendment has its own requirement). The strip is shared by every set on the animals and plants frontends and is not changed in place except by the Amend bar; a page that needs a different header switches the strip off and draws its own header in the set's template. The INS layout supports the strip, but no INS page uses it.
requirements.why: This is shared page chrome that already exists. The afternoon ruling keeps it as it is for every set: a page that needs another header switches it off, and only the Amend bar changes it in place. Each page's use of it belongs to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-026 to p1-030 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-023 to p1-027 render the strip, and a page can leave it out (repo-insfrontend-p4-022).

requirements.statement: Every page's footer on every frontend offers 'Privacy', 'Cookies' and 'Accessibility statement' links to the GOV.UK help pages, with the OGL v3.0 licence line and Crown copyright. The service has no cookies page, privacy notice or accessibility statement of its own.
requirements.why: This is the shared footer, and it already exists on both frontends.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-031 to p1-033, repo-insfrontend-p4-023 to p4-025 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-028 to p1-030 render the footer links.

requirements.statement: No page shows a cookie banner.
requirements.why: This is how the service is today. No source asks for a banner.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-033 shows no cookie banner on any page walked.

requirements.statement: Pages on every frontend are in English, with no language toggle. Copy falls back to English, and each copy file has a Welsh twin with the same keys and no empty values. The shared Welsh copy is an unreviewed machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off. Plants' first release is English-only with html lang en, and no Welsh is invented for it.
requirements.why: This is how the shared copy works today on both frontends. Design Release 2.1 has no Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-034 to p1-036, repo-insfrontend-p4-028 to p4-030 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-033 to p1-037 describe the copy.

requirements.statement: Every page offers the standard GOV.UK 'Skip to main content' link, targeting #main-content.
requirements.why: This is a GOV.UK accessibility requirement, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-030 records the link.

requirements.statement: No page shows who is signed in: no email, name or 'signed in as' strip, and no 'Sign out' link apart from the navigation's Log out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's header and navigation show no signed-in identity, and both frontends already match.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-039, trace-e2e-p1-040 and repo-insfrontend-p4-117 show no identity.

requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends, when sign-in fails the user sees a page titled 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in' and headed 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.', asking them to 'Please try again', where 'try again' links to sign-in.
requirements.why: A failed Defra ID sign-in is an authentication case the prototype cannot express, and the page already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-040 and p1-041 give the animals page, and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-064 the plants page.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, a failed sign-in shows the unauthorised page: browser title 'Unable to sign in', heading 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.' and body 'Please try again.', where 'try again' links to /auth/sign-in. The page has no back link. It is shown when the Defra ID callback fails, the token carries no organisation or fails verification, or the user's role and permissions cannot be loaded.
requirements.why: These are authentication failures the prototype cannot express, and the page already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-080 and p4-083 to p4-086 give the page and when it shows.

requirements.statement: An error response on every frontend is shown as the shared error page with the error's own HTTP status. The page's large heading is the status number, and a paragraph below it, which is also the browser title, reads 'Page not found' (404), 'Forbidden' (403), 'You need to sign in to view this page' (401), 'There is a problem with your request' (400) or 'Something went wrong' (any other). It shows no back link. An error on a path inside a journey set, routed or not, uses that set's chrome; a path under no set uses set-free chrome whose home link is the root.
requirements.why: Real errors are a constraint the prototype cannot express, and both frontends already share this page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-042 to p1-048, repo-insfrontend-p4-072 to p4-078 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-057 to p1-063 render the page.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, the service root / sends a signed-in user to the default set's dashboard, /live-animals.
requirements.why: This is how the animals frontend reaches its home today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-047 records the redirect.

requirements.statement: The shared notification actions read 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' on the animals and plants frontends. After a copy, a success message titled 'Notification copied' reads 'A new draft notification has been created.' After a delete, one titled 'Notification deleted' reads 'The notification has been deleted.' This shared copy is never reworded in place: a page whose wording differs adds keys in its feature's own copy.
requirements.why: This is shared copy the lists and notification pages already use, and the afternoon ruling forbids rewording it in place because the notification list uses it too. Comparing it with Design Release 2.1 belongs to the dashboard and notification-actions areas.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-055 to p1-058 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-065 and p1-066 give the copy.

requirements.statement: Address pickers offer a shared 'Add a new address' link. When a chosen address is not in the user's address book, the error reads 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.' When the address book cannot be reached, it reads 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: This is shared copy the journey's address pickers already use. Comparing the pickers with Design Release 2.1 belongs to the addresses area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-059 to p1-061 give the copy.

requirements.statement: Sign-in hands off to Defra ID with an OpenID Connect authorisation-code request (scope openid offline_access, query response mode, policy b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi), naming each frontend's own serviceId and its own /auth/sign-in-oidc callback. On success, the user's organisation, CRN and name are taken from the token and held in a server-side session.
requirements.why: Real sign-in through Defra ID is an authentication constraint the prototype's sign-in page cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-002 to p1-004 and trace-e2e-p15-012 record the handoff.

requirements.statement: After signing in, a user who belongs to more than one organisation is asked by Defra ID to 'Choose your organisation' from radios labelled with each organisation's name and SBI. A user with one organisation never sees that choice. The chosen organisation reaches the service through the sign-in callback, and the user lands on the page they asked for. No page in the service offers a way to switch organisation, and a page that needs an organisation returns 403 when the session has none.
requirements.why: Organisation choice is part of real Defra ID authentication, which the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p15-016 to p15-020 record the single-organisation and multi-organisation paths on the INS frontend.

requirements.statement: Signing in to one frontend signs the user in to the others without asking for credentials again, because Defra ID answers their requests straight away. Each frontend keeps its own session cookie on the shared host (sid for animals, ins-sid for INS, plants-sid for plants, all HttpOnly), so all three sessions are kept side by side. Each service has its own landing page after sign-in.
requirements.why: Moving between the animals journey and the INS dashboard and address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express. It already works.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p15-111 and p15-113 prove single sign-on and kept sessions across the three frontends. Whether signing out of one ends the others is not proven (repo-tests-p4-111-m1).

requirements.statement: A session is valid only while it is in the server-side cache (Redis when deployed). The session cookie lasts 4 hours and is HttpOnly. An expired token is refreshed when refresh is on, and otherwise the user is treated as signed out. Every route needs a signed-in user unless it opts out.
requirements.why: Real sessions are an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already work this way.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-031 and p1-032 record the cookies, and repo-insfrontend-p4-102 and p4-103 the session rules. What a user sees when a session lapses is not recorded (trace-e2e-p1-062).

requirements.statement: In stub mode the INS frontend signs a user in at once with no sign-in page, as 'Stub User' in the organisation given by an organisationId parameter (default 'stub-org-1'). The stub session lasts four hours, sign-out goes straight to /, and the Defra ID callback and organisation routes do not exist. Stub mode is refused in production.
requirements.why: This is how the INS frontend runs locally and in its own browser tests. It is part of today's real authentication set-up.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-106 to p4-113 give the stub mode.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, every form post must carry a valid CSRF token (except under /health, /assets and /public). Every page carries the token in a csrf-token meta tag, every form has a hidden 'crumb' input, and the CSRF cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite Strict.
requirements.why: Protection against cross-site request forgery is a real security constraint, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-033-m1, repo-insfrontend-p4-114 to p4-116 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-031 show the token.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy on its pages, redirects and sign-in callback. It limits scripts, styles, fonts, images and the base URL to its own origin (plus one hashed inline script), lets forms post to itself and the address book origin, and forbids framing and plugins. It also sends Strict-Transport-Security for a year, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Download-Options noopen, X-XSS-Protection and Cache-Control no-cache.
requirements.why: Security headers are a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already exist.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-052 to p1-060 record the headers.

requirements.statement: Security-header and cookie defects found on the way are not fixed by this programme: the CSP's connect-src lists 'wss' without a colon, the animals frontend sends no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP or COEP header, and the animals and plants frontends share one 'crumb' CSRF cookie on localhost.
requirements.why: These are problems in today's services that bringing the services up to Design Release 2.1 does not touch. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The Defra ID stub's own pages are not changed by this programme: its sign-in page ('Sign in using Government Gateway', user ID and password, 'Help signing in', the 'I have forgotten my password' placeholder, the CRN error message and its non-standard error summary), its title, phase banner and doubled service name, its signed-out page and its own security headers.
requirements.why: The stub stands in for Defra ID and is not one of the programme's repos. Its defects go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's accessibility suite holds every scanned page to WCAG 2.2 AA. It runs axe with the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa tags and fails on any violation, attaching a report per page. Only justified upstream or not-owned defects are excluded: govuk-frontend's conditional-reveal aria-expanded and the sign-in stub's error list. The suite scans selected states, tagged @a11y.
requirements.why: Every page this programme changes must keep passing this suite. It already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-001 to p6-020 define the suite.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite walks the live-animals journey from the dashboard to the submitted page and scans every journey page, both on initial load and with its answers filled.
requirements.why: This is the existing end-to-end accessibility proof of the journey. Each page Design Release 2.1 changes must still pass it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-021 and p6-042 define the two walks.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite scans the error summary state on the origin, CPH number, arrival details, transited countries and declaration pages, and the edit address details page.
requirements.why: This is the existing accessibility proof of the shared error summary on journey pages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-054 to p6-060 define the scans.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite also scans the import reason reveals, the private transporter pages, the commercial transporter register, the dashboard (populated, sorted, searched, paged, and at 320 by 568 and 568 by 320), review, submitted review, confirmation, the cancel-amendment and delete confirmations, the copied-address edit page, the contact page and the sign-in page.
requirements.why: This is the existing accessibility proof of the rest of the animals service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-062 to p6-087 define the scans.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's own browser tests check that a captioned page and the dashboard with its service navigation have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA violations. They exclude govuk-frontend's conditional-reveal false positive. The INS frontend checks every page's initial render and validation-error state against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 AA. The plants frontend checks every page's initial and error states with axe using the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa tags, with a Lighthouse accessibility floor of 0.70, and builds pages from govuk-frontend components only.
requirements.why: These are the existing in-repo accessibility checks that a navigation or layout change must keep passing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-013 and p1-026 record the passing animals checks, repo-insfrontend-p4-167 the INS checks and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-147 the plants checks.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's accessibility proof are not closed by this programme. The INS dashboard, sign-in and address book have no WCAG scan in the tests repo. The dashboard's copy action, the amending overview and an uploaded document are not scanned. Only five pages' error states are scanned, and only the dashboard at narrow viewports. No INS browser test proves sign-out, the unauthorised page, the error page or the banner and footer links.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suites, not differences from Design Release 2.1. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's security suite runs a traffic-driven OWASP ZAP scan of the animals frontend, animals admin, INS frontend, animals backend and address book API. Playwright drives real signed-in journeys through it: sign-in and sign-out on both frontends, change mode, reveals, dashboard search, sort and paging, document upload, amend, copy, cancel and delete, submission, and the INS address book lifecycle. The run fails on any FAIL-rated alert, a capped scan or an unreached context. The active scan is refused on CDP.
requirements.why: Every route this programme adds or changes must be driven through this scan to be attacked. The suite already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-090 to p6-123 define the suite.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's security scan are not closed by this programme. Plants has no security specs. The accepted path of the address book hand-off is not attacked. The animals copied-address edit page is not driven. The INS dashboard is in the scan only as a bare GET.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suite, not differences from Design Release 2.1. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo signs each worker in once and reuses the session. Its sign-in and cross-service tests start with no stored session. It keeps the sign-in password out of traces, and it sends only internet-bound calls through the CDP proxy.
requirements.why: Any new end-to-end proof of sign-in or navigation has to work within these existing suite rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-182 and p4-110 give the session rules.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend serves a fixed list of routes, all behind sign-in: the dashboard at /, and the address book list, add, view, edit and delete pages. It also serves /health, /auth/* and static files, plus a dev-only address lookup spike. It owns no journey, notification editing, upload or event publishing, and no database. Its target direction is to become the front door for every journey.
requirements.why: This is the shell that the dashboard, templates and address book pages Design Release 2.1 changes are added to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-119 and p4-124 list the routes.

requirements.statement: Each INS dashboard row links out to the animals frontend, which owns that notification: to /notifications/{reference}, or to .../notification-view when it is submitted. Only the animals journey is linked today.
requirements.why: This is how the INS dashboard hands off across services today. Design Release 2.1's dashboard is weighed in the dashboard area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-127 and p4-128 give the links.

requirements.statement: The INS dashboard at / is not scoped to the user's organisation: a signed-in user sees every organisation's notifications. This area does not fix that.
requirements.why: Organisation scoping of the dashboard is an authorisation defect owned by the dashboard area and an existing security ticket, not a layout or sign-in change. It goes to the report.

requirements.statement: The INS address book always sends the signed-in organisation to the address book API, and refuses to call it with none. Its ids are 24-character hex, and an unknown or deleted id gives 404. API field errors are mapped back to the form. Only the nine validated address fields are saved. The country list comes from reference data with GB first. A success banner shows once. A journey hand-off (journeyType, notificationId, fulfilmentId, handshakeToken) returns to the animals frontend for 'gbn-ag'.
requirements.why: These are the real persistence, validation and authorisation rules behind the address book that the navigation leads to. The address book area weighs its pages against Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-136 to p4-145 give the rules, and the smoke tests p4-180 to p4-182 prove them.

requirements.statement: Every change to the INS frontend follows its build rules. It stays in the govuk-frontend toolbox and keeps its four import boundaries. Each new page gets a URL builder, a route-list entry, English and Welsh copy with tests, unit tests mocked only at the network boundary, a browser test with axe checks and a Lighthouse audit. Format, lint, unit and browser suites must all pass, with cross-repo branches sharing one name. Every outside call is measured.
requirements.why: Templates and the navigation change land in the INS frontend, and these are the rules it holds every change to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-158, p4-163 and p4-163-m1 state the rules.

requirements.statement: Drift in the INS frontend's documentation and dependencies is not fixed by this programme. The workspace page names INS_MODE and AUTH_STUB_MODE where the repo uses STUB_MODE, and Vite where the repo uses webpack. It also calls the README template text when the README now describes the service. Some code imports Joi without declaring it as a dependency.
requirements.why: These are housekeeping defects, not differences from Design Release 2.1. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: DR1 judgements and DR1 build notes that meet no Design Release 2.1 difference in this area build nothing here. These are the section-caption rows, the navigation row's details, the return-control rename and rule (b) on which pages end with the return controls, the animals admin app keeping its own 'Sign out', and the notes on how the DR1 union backlog was run, numbered, banded, deferred and verified. Each stands only where its own area finds the real frontend and Design Release 2.1 clashing on that same difference.
requirements.why: The owner's ruling makes the DR1 parity backlog a source of judgements, never of requirements. Nothing is built because DR1 says so on its own.

requirements.statement: The performance suite signs in as a browser does: it follows a frontend's redirect chain through that frontend's /auth/sign-in, the Defra ID stub's sign-in form (posting the stub identity's CRN 2100010101 and a password) and /auth/callback back to the page asked for. It counts any hop through /auth/, an identity-provider path containing /oauth2/ or /idphub/, or /organisations as sign-in, counts a chain that lands with 200 without showing the form as sign-in, and never counts one that ends in a server error. It tags the post 'sign-in' and any later sign-in as re-authentication, checks that the INS sign-in went through Defra ID, and shares one cookie jar between the INS frontend and the journey frontend so the INS sign-in carries over to the live-animals dashboard.
requirements.why: This programme changes no sign-in route, so the suite's sign-in handling must keep working. A change to the /auth/ routes, the callback or the cross-frontend single sign-on would break it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-perftests-p2-005 to p2-009 and p1-079-m1 give the sign-in handling, and p1-080-m1 the shared cookie jar. The reframed live-animals list stays at the set root, so the dashboard the suite lands on after sign-in does not move (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-070, c-layout-and-sign-in-002).

requirements.statement: Every frontend page keeps what the performance suite reads off the page chrome: the CSRF token in the csrf-token meta tag, and on a notification page the hidden concurrencyToken input in its POST form. The suite posts forms url-encoded through the last POST form that holds a concurrencyToken (or the first POST form when none does), with its hidden fields. A stale concurrency token answered with a redirect counts as handled, and a request that is still redirecting after 10 hops fails its check.
requirements.why: Layout changes this programme makes must not drop the token meta tag, the concurrency token or the stale-notification redirect that the performance suite relies on (req-1715, req-1696).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-perftests-p2-010 to p2-013 read the tokens and post the forms that today's frontends render (repo-frontend-p1-001-m1, p1-025).

requirements.statement: The performance suite's 'INS signed-in page' readiness probe passes when the INS home at / answers 200 signed in with the main heading the home now shows, 'Import notification service', instead of 'Dashboard'. The 'address book read' probe keeps the heading 'Address book'. The stack is still ready only when one pass succeeds for all six probes.
requirements.why: The INS home's main heading changes from 'Dashboard' to 'Import notification service' to match Design Release 2.1 (c-146). The probe matches the heading exactly, so without this change every performance run would fail readiness after 300 seconds.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the probe passes only when / shows the heading 'Dashboard' (repo-perftests-p2-040). It must change in trade-imports-performance-tests in the same increment that changes the INS home's heading.

requirements.statement: The performance suite's run rules stand: every route it requests is named in its endpoint catalogue or the run fails; readiness is judged by real functional reads (reference-data /countries answering a non-empty array, and the backend notification reads), tagged 'readiness' to keep them out of every threshold; locally it reaches each service on its workspace-stack port (or LOCALHOST_ALIAS, or a <SERVICE_NAME>_URL), follows the frontends' absolute localhost redirects and injects Service Bus faults through toxiproxy; on CDP it uses each service's cdp-int URL, sends backend calls from a laptop through the protected gateway with DEVELOPER_API_KEY, and refuses to run against production. The catalogue names only the live-animals and address book pages the suite drives: a row that changes the suite adds every route its changed scripts newly request, and no row adds germinal-products routes.
requirements.why: Any change this programme makes to the suite has to work within these rules. Ruling 2026-10-09 claim 199 brings the suite into each row whose change breaks one of its k6 scripts (c-225). The list reframe keeps the list at the live-animals set root, so it moves no route the suite requests (c-layout-and-sign-in-002).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-perftests-p2-051 to p2-056 and p2-042-m1, p2-042-m2 give the rules today.

requirements.statement: Every page of the germinal-products set, mounted at /germinal-products in the animals frontend, carries the same shared page chrome as the live-animals set: the 'Import notification service' service navigation with the same items in the same order, the Alpha phase banner, the footer, the '<page> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' title pattern, section captions, back links, error summary and banners. The service name and the Dashboard item link to the germinal set's own root (/germinal-products), which renders the set's own notification list, and Dashboard stays current on every page inside a germinal notification. An error on a path under /germinal-products is shown in the germinal set's chrome, with its home link to that root.
requirements.why: Germinal products is its own sibling set beside live-animals, with its own journey, routes and services, so the set-scoped parts of the chrome (the home link, the current item, error-page chrome) must resolve inside it. The shared layout already resolves them per set.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists today. The shared layout already resolves the home link and current item inside the request's set (repo-frontend-p1-006, p1-010, p1-048-m1). The germinal list at the set root is the germinal-products theme's copy of the reframed live-animals list (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-087).

requirements.statement: A signed-in user's service navigation reads, in order, Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account and Log out on every frontend: both animals sets, the INS frontend and the plants frontend. Templates sits after Dashboard, links to Manage templates, and is marked as the current item on the templates pages, as Dashboard and Address book are on theirs. Every label keeps a Welsh copy entry beside the English one, as 'Dangosfwrdd', 'Llyfr cyfeiriadau', 'Rheoli cyfrif' and 'Allgofnodi' do today.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds Templates as the second item. The owner's templates ruling says templates go ahead now and that plants' navigation gets the item too, linking across to Manage templates. Log out stays last for the authentication reason c-212 gives.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every frontend offers four items, Dashboard, Address book, Manage account and Log out, with no Templates (repo-frontend-p1-008, repo-insfrontend-p4-006, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-007 to p1-010, trace-e2e-p15-002).

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, the Address book navigation item keeps today's destination. Plants is not wired to the INS address book, so this programme does not point the item at it.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps plants off the INS address book, and where plants' Address book link goes is a decision parked with the plants service owner.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p1-008 renders the item with the address book URL the page supplies, and its home stays parked with the service owner (repo-plantsfrontend-p9-141).

requirements.statement: Every page on every frontend shows a GOV.UK phase banner with a grey 'Alpha' tag reading 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.', where 'give your feedback by email' is the link. Its Welsh copy sits beside the English ('Alffa', 'rhowch eich adborth drwy e-bost').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows an Alpha banner, and DR1 judged the banner onto every page. All three frontends already show it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-015 and p1-016, repo-insfrontend-p4-015 and p4-016, and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-012 and p1-013 render the banner.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, a page with errors shows a GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem' ('Mae problem' in Welsh) at the top of the content, above the caption and heading. It lists one entry per field, carrying the first failing rule's message, each linking to its field or, where a page asks, to another page. Each field shows the same message inline. The summary takes focus when shown, except on a page that shows it without the user having just been refused. A page with no errors shows none.
requirements.why: This is the GOV.UK error pattern every page shares, and it already exists. Each page's own messages against Design Release 2.1 belong to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-050 to p1-054, repo-insfrontend-p4-068 to p4-071 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-044 to p1-048 render the summary, and trace-animals-fit-p1-005 shows it rendered.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user who opens any page of a frontend is sent through sign-in, with the page asked for (path and query) carried in a redirect parameter. After signing in they return to that page, or to the frontend's dashboard home when none was asked for. Only a relative path on the same service is followed, once; anything else goes to the home. A draft's saved answers are still there after signing out and back in.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pretend sign-in always lands on its dashboard. The real services send the user back to where they were going, a real authentication behaviour the prototype cannot express, and it already works.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-001, p1-029, p1-048 and p1-049 show the animals round trip back to the page asked for, trace-e2e-p15-013 and p15-017 the INS one, and repo-insfrontend-p4-088 to p4-092 the INS rules.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, every page's browser title reads the page's title, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - ', as on the animals frontend. It changes in the same increment that changes the INS frontend's titles to that pattern.
requirements.why: The INS frontend's pipe titles change to the GOV.UK pattern (req-1686). Plants has the same pipe pattern, and the owner's rule is that a change to something plants also has changes plants in the same increment, mirroring wording patterns.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants' titles read '<page title> | Import notification service' (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-001).

requirements.statement: The live-animals set's notification list at its root has the browser title 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', instead of repeating the service name, as the reframed list takes the 'Dashboard' title. Plants' own list takes the same title in the same increment.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling gives the reframed list the 'Dashboard' title and reframes plants' list in the same increments.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list's title is 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK', because its page name is the service name (trace-e2e-p1-033, trace-animals-fit-p1-003).

requirements.statement: The shared status strip's tag for a notification being amended reads 'Amend' instead of 'Amending'. It changes once, in the shared strip, so every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants) shows it at the same time, and the end-to-end specs that read 'Amending' change with it.
requirements.why: The owner's 9 October afternoon ruling changes the label in every set at once as part of the Amend bar, the one change allowed to the shared strip itself.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip shows a yellow 'Amending' tag on both journey frontends (repo-frontend-p1-029, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-026), and the security scan's amend walk reads it (repo-tests-p6-116).

requirements.statement: The plants frontend's high-risk plants set is mounted at /high-risk-plants. Its dashboard is the base path, a new notification is created at /notifications, each overview is at /notifications/{journeyId} and each journey page answers GET and POST at /notifications/{journeyId}/{slug}, all rendered in the shared layout with the service's own stylesheet and ES-module script. Every route passes the set's entry guard and needs a signed-in session. A path belongs to the set whose mount it falls under, and /health and /auth/* belong to none. The set keeps its known notifications, opening run and flow-only answers in session cookies, and refuses to start with required configuration missing or with impure or unbound obligations.
requirements.why: This is the plants shell that every mirrored change lands in. It already exists, and the programme keeps plants' architecture as it is.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p1-039 to p1-042 and p1-085 to p1-096 describe the set as it is today.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, a question page the overview links to directly ends with three controls: the primary button ('Save and continue' unless the page names its own), a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button that saves and goes to the overview, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that leaves without saving. A page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone. A page opened from check your answers carries ?change=1 and returns there after saving. Otherwise the next page is the next one in the opening run while it lasts, then the next one in the same section. The hub is headed 'Overview', and 'hub' never shows to users.
requirements.why: These are plants' save actions and return paths, built to the same rule as the animals frontend. Rows that change them, such as the lenient save and the amend endings, change plants in their own increments.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p1-067 to p1-072 give the page endings, and p1-049 to p1-052 the return destinations.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, a date is one text input about ten characters wide, in d/m/yyyy form, with a small bold label and an optional hint. A date that does not match is kept as typed and shown back in the field. A date field can add the MoJ date picker, limited to an earliest and latest date.
requirements.why: This is the shared date field of plants' page kit. It already exists, and no row in this area changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p1-073 to p1-075 describe the field.

requirements.statement: On the plants frontend, Defra ID sign-in is the only precondition to notifying: there is no registration page, registration check or onboarding step, and any signed-in organisation reaches the dashboard. Sign-in is enforced on every route, in stub mode too, and internal-user login is not part of this frontend.
requirements.why: Sign-in is a real authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, and plants' owner has already ruled it this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-081 and p9-082 record the ruling as built.

requirements.statement: Plants' parked chrome decisions are not settled by this programme: its service name, feedback address, helpdesk contact lines, the homes of the Address book and Manage account links, the footer's accessibility statement and privacy notice URLs, the confirmation page's provisional help block, and moving its English-only unauthorised view into the copy files.
requirements.why: They wait on the plants service owner, not on Design Release 2.1. The programme mirrors the animals frontend's chrome, which plants already matches.

conflicts.about: Whether the service navigation keeps a Log out item: Design Release 2.1 drops it, and the real services have it.

positions.says: In DR2.1 the service navigation has no Log out item, unlike design release 2.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as authentication, overrides the prototype default.
DR1 judged that sign-out sits in the service navigation as 'Log out', replacing the separate 'Sign out' link.
The Log out navigation item links to /auth/sign-out.

conflicts.outcome: Log out stays as the last navigation item on every frontend: both animals sets, the INS frontend and the plants frontend (req-969, req-1674, req-layout-and-sign-in-001). The prototype has no real session to end, so leaving it out does not show a decision about sign-out. In the real services, Log out is the only way to end a Defra ID session, and the ruling lets an authentication constraint override the prototype. The rest of the prototype's list (Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account) is adopted, so prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-021 and p1-018 still back the Templates requirement. Only the claim that drops Log out is set aside.

conflicts.about: Where the Address book navigation item goes: inside the same service in Design Release 2.1, or the INS frontend's address book in the real services.

positions.says: Under DR2.1 the address book sits under the service's own base path, at /design-release-2.1/address-book.
Rhys ruled that the dashboard and the address book are temporary in the animals frontend and move to trade-imports-ins-frontend.
Cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default.
The prototype never decides architecture: the split into services and URL paths stay the real services'.
c-213 is kept for a real constraint or a DR1 judgement.

conflicts.outcome: The Address book item goes to the INS frontend's address book from the animals frontend, in both animals sets, and from the INS frontend (req-1677). The address book is a shared capability in a separate service, which the single-service prototype cannot express, and the owner's later ruling keeps this conflict and says the prototype never decides services or URL paths. The prototype claim that places it under the service's own base is set aside. The item, its label and its place in the order still stand. Plants is not wired to the INS address book, so its item keeps today's destination (req-layout-and-sign-in-002). Rhys's DR1 judgement still moves the address book to the INS frontend, though the 9 October afternoon and templates rulings keep the notification lists in their own frontends (c-layout-and-sign-in-001).

conflicts.about: Where the GOV.UK header logo and the service name link: Design Release 2.1 sends both to its index of design releases, which has no counterpart in a real service.

positions.says: The GOV.UK logo links to the service index (/design-release-2.1/index), and the service name in the service navigation does too.
On DR2.1 pages the header logo and the service name both link to the prototype index.
The GOV.UK header logo links to https://www.gov.uk/.
The service name links to the set's dashboard at /live-animals.
The GOV.UK header logo links to https://www.gov.uk/.
A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
c-214 is kept for a real constraint or a DR1 judgement.

conflicts.outcome: Keep the current targets, as the owner's later ruling confirms. The GOV.UK logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ on every frontend, as the GOV.UK header pattern does. The service name links to the dashboard home of the set or frontend the page belongs to: /live-animals on live-animals pages, /germinal-products on germinal-products pages, /high-risk-plants on plants pages and / on the INS frontend. Each set root renders its own notification list (c-layout-and-sign-in-001). The prototype sends both links to its index of design releases, which is prototype tooling that is not built (req-1681), so it names no real destination to move them to; the prototype keeps a separate Dashboard item, so its index is not a stand-in for the dashboard. With no DR1 judgement on the header links, the real frontends' targets are the only buildable ones and stand.

conflicts.about: Where the phase banner's feedback link goes: a placeholder '#' in Design Release 2.1, or the APHA service desk mailbox in the real services.

positions.says: DR2.1 dashboard pages show an Alpha phase banner whose feedback link is a placeholder '#'.
Because the design's feedback link is a placeholder, DR1 ruled it to be mailto:APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk, and forbade inventing a /feedback route or survey URL.
The phase banner's feedback link is an email link to the APHA service desk.

conflicts.outcome: The feedback link stays mailto:APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk on every frontend, plants included (req-1684). DR1 already judged this same difference, a placeholder feedback link in the design, and a DR1 judgement on the same difference outranks the prototype. The INS and plants frontends already use the same destination. The Alpha banner itself is shown by today's claims (req-layout-and-sign-in-003), so setting aside the prototype's placeholder claim loses nothing.

conflicts.about: Whether service pages show the signed-in user's email and 'Home' and 'About' links, as the tests repo's shared page object suggests.

positions.says: The signed-in user's email or name is shown nowhere, and there is no 'Sign out' link outside the navigation's Log out.
Every service page offers Home, About, Log out, Address book and Dashboard links and shows the signed-in user's email (inferred from the shared base page object).

conflicts.outcome: No page shows the signed-in identity (req-1702). The frontend outranks the tests repo, the end-to-end traces show no identity (trace-e2e-p1-040), and the tests repo's own dashboard spec asserts no email (repo-tests-p4-057). The base page object's Home, About and email locators are stale helpers that no spec asserts. They can be removed whenever the tests repo is next touched.

conflicts.about: Whether each animals set's root hands the user on to a notification list in the INS frontend or renders the set's own list.

positions.says: With the list staying in the animals frontend, each set's root renders its own list, replacing 'each set's root redirects to its INS list'.
The live animals list stays in the animals frontend, and the earlier move to the INS frontend is superseded.
There is no backend list filter by category; each set's root redirects to its INS list.
Rhys ruled that the dashboard and the address book are temporary in the animals frontend and move to the INS frontend.

conflicts.outcome: Each set's root renders its own notification list: /live-animals, /germinal-products and plants' /high-risk-plants. The two later 9 October rulings outrank the morning ruling and withdraw its redirect, so the service name, the Dashboard item and every return to the dashboard keep pointing at the set root, which is the list itself (req-1676, req-1907). Rhys's DR1 judgement is set aside only for the notification list: it still moves the address book to the INS frontend (c-213, req-1677), so that claim is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether the performance suite joins the notification list's reframe because the live-animals set root stops rendering the list.

positions.says: The reframed list stays at the live-animals set root, and the k6 suite's list request does not move.
trade-imports-performance-tests joins inc-129 because inc-129 moves a route its scripts use: the set root stops rendering the list.
The suite opens the live-animals dashboard at /live-animals, through sign-in when signed out.

conflicts.outcome: The list stays at /live-animals, so the reframe moves no route the suite requests, and the suite does not join it for a route move (req-1903, req-1906). The suite still changes in any increment that changes what its scripts read, under c-225's rule, which ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-199 also states; that part of the claim still stands, so it is not overruled.
